body:
Triage (objectui finding round): promoted to `pm:queue` · `domain:ui` · type Task. Newly actionable by inheritance: the #5301 maintainer ruling (2026-08-20) settled the write-back rule for the sibling surface, and PR #5427 shipped `setLocalized` in `@object-ui/i18n` — the designer's read-only branch was waiting on exactly that rule. Scope: adopt `setLocalized` for `DashboardEditor`'s widget-title input (active-locale write-back, others preserved), fix the two stale doc comments (the `isAuthorableTitle` premise and the dangling #4163 deferral), and cover `DashboardWidgetInspector`'s identical placeholder in the same pass — same file family, same rule, one dispatch. ⛔ A full multi-locale editor stays out of scope; if the dev believes it is needed, that is a new decision card. S–M, `mode:subagent`, opus; Clause-②: no.

**Claim:** `domain:ui` execution seat, session `session_012u2pRjcqAYtoEjgr3wwhnK` · branch `claude/issue-5428-dashboard-title-locale-writeback` · round 4.

## ⛔ Correction to the triage note: this is NOT one file family, it is two packages

Triage says to cover `DashboardWidgetInspector`'s identical placeholder "in the same pass — same file family". The two surfaces are in **different packages**, measured on `origin/main`:

```
packages/plugin-designer/src/DashboardEditor.tsx
packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/DashboardWidgetInspector.tsx
```

The one-dispatch decision still holds — same rule, same stale premise — but plan it as a **cross-package diff** with two changesets' worth of impact, not a single-package edit. `@object-ui/app-shell` and `@object-ui/plugin-designer` are both published.

## Both premises verified

`DashboardEditor.tsx` — the guard is at `:300` / `:304` / `:307`, `isAuthorableTitle` defined at `:152`, and the dangling #4163 deferral at `:292`.

`DashboardWidgetInspector.tsx:233-250` carries the identical placeholder **and the identical stale premise**, verbatim:

> Nothing in any corpus can hit this path yet — `I18nLabel` was plain `string` through 17.0.0-rc.5, so no stored widget title can (…) (objectui#4163, part 2)

That is the claim the card shows is expired: rc.6 is the pinned version, and the same file family already says so elsewhere. Fix the comment as well as the branch — a stale justification left in place is how this recurred.

## Scope, per triage

Adopt `setLocalized` from `@object-ui/i18n` (shipped by PR #5427 under the #5301 ruling): a save writes back **only the active locale's entry and preserves the others**. Both surfaces, same rule.

⛔ **A full multi-locale editor stays out of scope.** If you conclude it is needed, that is a new decision card — say so in the report, do not build it. Clause ②: not tripped (`isAuthorableTitle` is module-local, no new exports) — but if your implementation adds an export to either package, stop and report before landing.

The pin that matters is the data-preservation one: editing in one locale must leave every other locale's entry byte-identical. A "the input is no longer read-only" assertion is green against a fix that flattens the map, which is precisely the data loss the read-only branch was protecting against.

## ACCEPT — PR #5588

Gates read **by name** on head `69335280e`, all 22 runs accounted for: `Test (shard 1/4)` `(2/4)` `(3/4)` `(4/4)`, `Type Check`, `Lint`, `Build & E2E`, `Build Docs`, `Bundle Analysis`, `Doc Snippet Type Check`, `Doc Component Type Check`, `Internal Docs Link Check`, `Changeset Declaration`, `Changeset Bump Policy`, `Changeset Fixed Group Check`, `Control Byte Scan`, `Skill Guide Path Check`, `Live E2E (informational)`, `label` — every one `completed: success`, plus the three `skipped` matrix no-ops. Console budget PASS; `plugin-designer` **shrank** 212.39 → 212.30 KB, consistent with removing the read-only branch and its dead classes.

### The premise came back stronger than the card

The card argues the "safe without a ruling" clause **expired** because rc.6 widened `I18nLabel`. You measured that the installed spec is **17.0.0 final**, with `I18nLabelSchema = z.union([z.string(), z.record(z.string(), z.string())])`. So the branch was not merely resting on a stale premise — it was actively denying an author the ability to edit a widget title in their own locale, on a runtime where map-valued titles are fully supported. That upgrades this from tidy-up to defect.

### My correction held, and you confirmed it independently

Triage called `DashboardWidgetInspector` "same file family" as `DashboardEditor`. They are in different published packages, which makes this a cross-package diff with two packages' worth of blast radius. You re-derived that rather than taking my word for it, which is the right instinct given three path errors in two rounds — one of them mine.

### The read/write pairing — I verified the justification rather than accepting it

This is the one genuinely subtle thing in the PR: `DashboardWidgetInspector` **reads** through the spec's `resolveI18nLabel` (which #4163's ruling requires of that package) and **writes** through objectui's `setLocalized`. Mixing two implementations across a read/write boundary is normally how drift starts.

Checked on `origin/main`:

```
packages/plugin-list/src/__tests__/i18nLabel-resolver-parity.test.ts:213
  it('has no rule divergence left — only the miss spelling differs (objectui#3907)')
packages/i18n/src/pickLocalized.ts:135
  export function setLocalized(
```

The parity suite holds the two resolvers limb for limb and pins that they differ **only** in how each spells a miss — and `setLocalized` always produces a hit for the locale it just wrote, so the miss spelling is unreachable on this path. The argument is sound, and adding round-trip assertions here rather than only citing the parity suite is what makes it check rather than claim.

### The pin is a preservation pin, which is the whole point

Every new assertion is about the **shape of what was written**, not about the input being enabled. That distinction is load-bearing and your ablation proves it: under the flattening mutation `onChange({ title: e.target.value })`, the *"shows a map-valued title resolved, and EDITABLE"* cases stayed **green** at both surfaces, while only the preservation assertions went red — 4 failed / 23 passed, red at both surfaces. That is the card's warning reproduced exactly: editability alone would have been a passing test over a data-loss fix.

Both directions of non-vacuity are covered too — editing under `zh-CN` leaves `en` alone (a fix hard-wired to `en` fails), an absent locale **adds** rather than overwrites, and a plain-string title stays a plain string (a fix that wrapped everything into a map fails).

### Scope

No new exports — `isAuthorableTitle` was module-local and `writeWidgetTitle` is too, so clause ② stays untripped. `@object-ui/i18n` untouched. The full multi-locale editor correctly stays out, and correctly is **not** re-pointed at another tracker: a comment aimed at a closed card is exactly how this premise survived, so replacing it with the rule actually in force is the right repair.

### Follow-ons

**#5590** (record-picker's `emptyText` drops the inline-locale-map arm, third package, same dead-tracker class) and **#5591** (two comments still name the closed #4163 as the live tracker, in `pickLocalized.ts:132` and `WidgetConfigPanel.tsx:518`). Both filed unassigned. Noting that `pickLocalized` was this card's read-only reuse target and was correctly left alone.

Proceeding to ready-for-review and the merge queue.
